svg.text: BasketBrief — architecture
A Strands agent chases the missing evidence, recalculates in code, and delivers an approved report to each donor. The model interprets; the code decides what is allowed.
Contributors
Rana · receipts and supplies —
and receipt photographs
Sami · delivery team — kit counts
and later corrections
Each has a role-scoped capability link;
nobody can answer or approve as another.
Amal · Coordinator
One page: the figures, the sources behind
them, what is unresolved, and the single
decision that is hers — approve this version.
She is not asked to relay messages.
Worker
New evidence queues a job. Before the
agent runs, every attached photograph
is transcribed — never a model choice.
Amazon Nova Pro · vision
Reads the receipt photograph → typed fields
Code adds the line items up against the
printed total; a disagreement is surfaced,
never corrected. Transcription = source text.
Strands Agents SDK — the BasketBrief agent
model → reasoning → tool call → tool result → … → a short account for the coordinator
Amazon Bedrock · Amazon Nova Pro
BedrockModel · us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 · temperature 0 · sequential tools · budget hook
The agent chooses the next tool

g.text: prepare_donor_reports → one draft per donor, from stored facts only

svg.text: Guards that live in code, not in the prompt
· An amount is recordable only if it literally appears in that source's text.
· A field the source does not state is dropped — it never costs the counts the source does state.
· Kits loaded, delivered, returned and unique households are four different facts.
· Source text is untrusted data: an instruction inside a message is evidence, not a command.
Follow-up gate — after the model's turn
Code recomputes the known gaps: unsupported spending, or a missing delivery count.
If one has no open question, the agent is handed it once and asks in its own words.
The promise "it follows up" therefore does not depend on the model remembering to.
A question already open is never asked a second time.
State — SQLite, versioned
evidence (immutable, with its transcription) · facts, each pinned to the
source that stated it · questions · report versions with a content hash ·
approvals · delivery intents · receipts · an append-only event log
Every number the coordinator and the donors see is read from here.
Report prose is written by the model; report figures never are.
A new source bumps the project revision, which marks dependent
drafts outdated and invalidates approvals bound to the old version.
Approval — the only human gate
The coordinator approves one exact version: report id + content hash +
revision + recipients. Unresolved items must be acknowledged explicitly.
If evidence changed in between, the approval is refused —
it cannot be reused for a version the coordinator never read.
Nothing reaches a donor without passing this check at dispatch time.
Donors — role-scoped inboxes
Northstar Foundation (English) · Community Giving Circle (Arabic)
Each receives the approved snapshot with its own delivery receipt and
can open only what was delivered to them — never another donor's copy,
and never a later draft that silently replaced what they read.
AgentCore Memory — the vendor ledger
A workspace lives for one distribution; a team does not. Vendors this team has
bought from before outlive every report here, so a vendor nobody has seen is a
review hint before it reaches a donor. Advisory: it never changes a number.
Live demo
basketbrief.mlki.app · FastAPI + Cloudflare Tunnel · a fresh workspace per visitor
a correction re-enters as new evidence: facts move, dependent reports redraft, the old approval stops working
One cycle, end to end
new evidence → photographs transcribed by Nova Pro → agent reads, records or defers each source → inspects the workspace → asks the one person who has the gap → drafts both donor reports
→ follow-up gate verifies nothing was left unasked → coordinator approves one exact version → delivered to each donor inbox with a receipt → a later correction starts the cycle again

AWS services used: Amazon Bedrock (Nova Pro, text and vision) and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory (the vendor ledger). All organisations, people, receipts and figures in the demo are fictional. Agents for Humans Hackathon · Good Neighbor Agents.
